L343@P5: in December 2005. Note, however, the gasoline and ethanol fuel
L344@P5: adjustment is not included in Mt and is treated explicitly.
L345@P5: This procedure is used directly to estimate total weekly inputs to
L346@P5: refineries and production. When refineries are closed or inoperable,
L347@P5: the lagged monthly data impacts the estimate of operable capacity
L348@P5: and percent utilization in the WPSR. Operable capacity is the
L349@P5: latest reported monthly operable capacity. The percent utilization
L350@P5: is calculated as gross weekly inputs divided by operable capacity.
L351@P5: The use of monthly capacity data may result in an overestimate of
L352@P5: operable capacity and an underestimate of percent utilization until the
L353@P5: shutdown is shown in the monthly data.
L354@P5: To estimate stocks of finished products, the preceding procedure
L355@P5: is followed separately for refineries, bulk terminals, and pipelines.
L356@P5: Total estimates are performed by summing over establishment types.
L357@P5: Published values of gasoline production include a fuel adjustment to
L358@P5: account for the imbalance between supply and disposition of motor
L359@P5: gasoline blending components and fuel ethanol. For further detail,
L360@P5: refer to Additional Sources of Data, Data Obtained from Supplemental
L361@P5: Sources (below).
L362@P5: Weekly imports data are highly variable on a company-by-company
L363@P5: basis or a week-to-week basis. Therefore, an exponentially smoothed
L364@P5: ratio has been developed for weekly imports. The estimate of total
L365@P5: weekly imports is the product of the smoothed ratio and the sum of
L366@P5: the weekly reported values and imputed values.
L367@P5: For imports, the ratio is smoothed as follows:
L368@P5: Rt
L369@P5:  = α * rt + (1 - α) * Rt-1
L370@P5: where
L371@P5: Rt is the smoothed ratio for week t+1 (using ratios through week
L372@P5: t),
L373@P5: rt is week t’s ratio of the most recent monthly total for all
L374@P5: respondents to the monthly total of respondents from the
L375@P5: weekly sample,
L376@P5: Rt-1 is the smoothed ratio for week t (using ratios through week t-1),
L377@P5: α is a number between 0 and 1, chosen by product but not by
L378@P5: PADD/Respondent ID.
L379@P5: When Ms = 0, then rt is not defined for the week and the smoothed
L380@P5: ratio is not updated, that is, the previous smoothed ratio is used as the
L381@P5: multiplier.
L382@P5: Macro Editing
L383@P5: After the respondent-level data have been collected and processed.
L384@P5: The WPSR processing system is “locked down” to all staff except
L385@P5: a select group of industry analysts and statisticians, referred to as
L386@P5: the WPSR Review Team. Aggregate-level estimates are generated
L387@P5: by product and geographic region for the current week, three prior
L388@P5: weeks, year ago data for the same week, along with 4-week averages.
L389@P5: The WPSR Review Team has the responsibility for reviewing the
L390@P5: aggregated data for all products and resolving inconsistencies with
L391@P5: these estimates.
L392@P5: Once the WPSR Review Team have completed their review,
L393@P5: preliminary WPSR tables are generated and provided to the
L394@P5: Petroleum Division Director (PDD) for review. At 4 p.m., the team
L395@P5: meets with the PDD for a final review and discussion of the estimates.
L396@P5: Discrepancies in the data are discussed and, if necessary, adjustments
L397@P5: are made and the final published statistics are generated for release on
L398@P5: Wednesday morning at 10:30 a.m.
L399@P5: Dissemination
L400@P5: The data are published in the WPSR and the TWIP every Wednesday
L401@P5: for the report period ending on the previous Friday. The WPSR tables
L402@P5: are released to the EIA Web site at 10:30 a.m. (Eastern Standard Time)
L403@P5: in CSV and XLS formats. The weekly highlights are released in PDF
L404@P5: format at 10:30 am. The entire WPSR is released at 1:00 p.m. in PDF
L405@P5: and HTML format. For weeks which include holidays (or have other
L406@P5: disruptions to normal operations), releases are delayed by one day.
L407@P5: The WPSR tables can be accessed at: http://www.eia.gov/petroleum/
L408@P5: supply/weekly/.
L409@P5: Selected data from the weekly supply surveys are also published in
L410@P5: the This Week in Petroleum (TWIP) generally available at 1:00 p.m.
L411@P5: Eastern Time on Wednesdays. The TWIP can be accessed at: http://
L412@P5: www.eia.gov/oog/info/twip/twip.asp.
L413@P5: Additional Sources of Data
L414@P5: Due to the tight time constraints in publishing weekly petroleum
L415@P5: supply statistics and the desire to reduce industry response burden,
L416@P5: some of the statistics published in the WPSR are obtained from
L417@P5: sources other than the 7 weekly supply surveys. These other sources
L418@P5: include models to data and data from supplemental sources such as
L419@P5-6: the PSM or the Bureau of the Census.38 Weekly Petroleum Status Report/Energy Information Administration
L420@P6: Data Obtained Through Models
L421@P6: Domestic Crude Oil Production (Tables 1 and 9)
L422@P6: EIA estimates weekly domestic crude oil production using a
L423@P6: combination of short-term forecasts and the latest available production
L424@P6: estimates from Alaska. The four data elements contributing to the
L425@P6: estimate are:
L426@P6: • the most recent Short-Term Energy Outlook (STEO)
L427@P6: model estimate (including interim estimates) for average
L428@P6: daily production for the lower 48 States and the Federal
L429@P6: Gulf of Mexico (GOM) (STEO Table 4a: http://www.eia.
L430@P6: gov/forecasts/steo/data.cfm?type=tables);
L431@P6: • daily production volumes delivered from the North
L432@P6: Slope of Alaska to the Trans-Alaska Pipeline System
L433@P6: (TAPS) (reported to EIA by the Alyeska Pipeline Service
L434@P6: Company);
L435@P6: • daily volumes of natural gas plant liquids produced
L436@P6: on the North Slope delivered to TAPS (reported to EIA
L437@P6: by BP); and
L438@P6: • daily production for South Alaska estimated from
L439@P6: monthly production reports (lagged by two months)
L440@P6: from the Alaska Oil and Gas Conservation Commission
L441@P6: (AOGCC).
L442@P6: Most of the uncertainty in the weekly estimate is associated with
L443@P6: the STEO forecast for lower 48 and GOM production. For example,
L444@P6: when lower 48 crude oil production is either increasing or decreasing
L445@P6: rapidly, the accuracy of the estimate for any particular month is likely
L446@P6: to be reduced. During tropical storms or hurricanes that affect Gulf of
L447@P6: Mexico oil production, near real-time daily shut-in volumes reported
L448@P6: by the Bureau of Safety and Environmental Enforcement (BSEE) are
L449@P6: subtracted from the daily lower 48 estimate. See Previous STEO
L450@P6: Forecasts at http://www.eia.gov/forecasts/steo/data.cfm?type=tables
L451@P6: for comparisons of current and previous monthly STEO forecasts
L452@P6: for lower 48 oil production and percent changes for STEO quarterly
L453@P6: forecasts.
L454@P6: The weekly estimates of domestic crude oil production are reviewed
L455@P6: monthly when the Short-Term Energy Outlook (STEO) is released
L456@P6: to identify differences with recent trends in survey-based domestic
L457@P6: production reported in the Petroleum Supply Monthly (PSM) and
L458@P6: other current data. If a large difference between the two series is
L459@P6: observed, the weekly production estimate may be re-benchmarked on
L460@P6: weeks when the STEO is released.
L461@P6: Exports (Tables 1, 7, and 9)
L462@P6: Official U.S. exports statistics for crude oil, petroleum products, and
L463@P6: biofuels are compiled and published by the U.S. Census Bureau each
L464@P6: month. EIA obtains these data on a monthly basis approximately six
L465@P6: weeks after the end of the monthly reporting period. Weekly exports
L466@P6: statistics for crude oil, petroleum products, and biofuels are obtained
L467@P6: through a memorandum of understanding with the U.S. Customs
L468@P6: and Border Protection (CBP) to access their Automated Commercial
L469@P6: Environment (ACE) system. Except for exports to Canada, all entities
L470@P6: exporting products from the United States are required to file export
L471@P6: information with ACE. EIA receives unedited data files from CBP each
L472@P6: week that EIA processes to remove duplicate entries and to convert
L473@P6: measurements as needed. This edited data is then used to estimate

L0: ### Revision/Correction
L1: 
L2: Weekly Petroleum Status Report Revision Notice
L3: 
L4: August 28, 2026
L5: On Wednesday, August 26, we published the full set of Weekly Petroleum Status Report (WPSR) data and WPSR summary text at 10:30 a.m. The summary text initially said distillate fuel inventories “increased by 2.2 million barrels.” In fact, distillate fuel inventories decreased by 2.2 million barrels, a change that was accurately reported in our data tables. We updated the text to accurately reflect the data at 12:13 p.m. on August 26.
L6: This revision notice should have been posted on the same day for full transparency and to clarify that only the text of the summary was erroneous, not the data tables. We regret the errors.

The correct percent change from 6/23/17 to 6/22/18 is 15%. This calculation has been updated in the PDF and CSV files.
